subject: Dedicated reservation — commitment hedge & burst architecture (Nimbus Therapeutics)
thread_summary: Initial proposal for a dedicated reservation with a commitment-hedge structure: three sizing options (conservative, balanced, aggressive), burst windows, warm pool strategy, activation triggers and billing smoothing. Follow-ups clarify burst billing, decommit windows, and finalize ramp schedule for LOI.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ari Goldstein <ari.goldstein@nimbusthera.com>, Nimbus Therapeutics <contracts@nimbusthera.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Dedicated reservation — commitment hedge & burst architecture (Nimbus Therapeutics)

Hi Ari / Nimbus team,

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation, attached is a proposal that focuses on predictable baseline capacity for your inference workloads while preserving headroom for spikes during model retrains and batch scoring. High-level notes:

- Goal: give Nimbus predictable unit economics for production inference while providing a low-friction way to burst for unplanned load (research experiments, release days).
- Key knobs: minimum committed GPUs (baseline), burst lanes (pre-warmed, billed differently), warm pool (short-term cache of running containers for <30 min bursts), and ramp triggers tied to usage/OKRs.

Proposal snapshot (see attached Nimbus_Reserve_Proposal_v1.xlsx for line-item pricing):

Option A — Conservative Hedge
  - Baseline: 16 x A100H (80GB) equivalent
  - Burst ceiling: up to 64 GPUs on demand for up to 72 hours/month
  - Ramp: 16 -> 24 after 3 months dependent on 80% baseline utilization
  - Monthly committed fee + burst overage (1.5x unit rate)

Option B — Balanced (recommended)
  - Baseline: 32 x A100H equiv.
  - Burst ceiling: up to 96 GPUs with reserved warm pool of 8 GPUs for fast bursts
  - Ramp: 32 -> 48 over 4 months with canary windows for new models
  - Pricing: blended committed rate with tiered overage pricing and quarterly smoothing credits

Option C — Aggressive Onramp
  - Baseline: 64 x A100H equiv.
  - Burst ceiling: up to 160 GPUs with dedicated H100 lanes for low-latency variants
  - Ramp: staged across 6 months; activation triggers include production SLA and 2x weekly peak tests

Operational & contractual highlights:
- Warm pool: short-lived pre-warmed instances that can bring startup time down to <90s for first token in model families.
- Canary & rollouts: canary pools for model rollouts and automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants on degradation.
- Decommit windows: standard 90-day decommit window for baseline reductions; we can negotiate a 60-day pilot term for initial ramp.
- Credits & smoothing: we propose a quarterly smoothing credit to help you absorb burst events during launch windows — details in the spreadsheet.

Next steps: please review Option B (recommended) and let us know 1) whether the baseline sizing aligns with your internal forecasts, 2) how you want burst billing to be handled (charged to commit vs separate charge), and 3) any procurement/legal timing constraints.

Attaching: Nimbus_Reserve_Proposal_v1.xlsx, SLA-terms.pdf

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call later this week to refine.

—Marcus

Thanks Marcus — good structure. A few clarifying questions before we run this through procurement and architecture: 

1) Burst billing: can you explain the difference between "burst overage (1.5x unit rate)" vs charging bursts against the committed pool? For our finance team, a single blended invoice is easier to forecast if possible.
2) Warm pool sizing: is the warm pool capacity billed as part of baseline or as a buffer? We run a lot of short-lived experiments and want to avoid cold starts without paying for a full reserved GPU all the time.
3) Decommit / flexibility: we have a stage roll to Beta in 4 months; do you offer a trial period to increase baseline temporarily without a long-term uplift?

Also cc'ing our contracts inbox (contracts@nimbusthera.com) — they'll want to see SLA language and the decommit timelines.

Ari — thanks for the questions, answered inline below and I've attached a v2 spreadsheet with alternative billing options (Nimbus_Reserve_Proposal_v2.xlsx).

1) Burst billing options (choose one):
  a) Separate overage (default): bursts above baseline billed at 1.5x committed unit rate; good for clear accounting separation.
  b) Blended invoice (finance-friendly): we amortize an estimated burst allowance into your monthly committed fee (reduces visible overage but requires a predictable forecast). If actual bursts exceed allowance, overflow is billed at standard overage. We can set a quarterly true-up.
  c) Commit + reservation credits: you can purchase a small reserved burst pool (e.g., 8 GPUs) that lives in a higher-cost lane but is included on the committed invoice. This gives a single invoice while keeping marginal control.

2) Warm pool billing: warm pool instances are billed as 'buffer' capacity at a discounted standby rate (roughly 35% of committed unit price). They are not charged as full committed GPUs; they only count against baseline when promoted to active GPUs (promotion happens automatically when latency impact is detected).

3) Trial / temporary uplift: we offer a 60-day pilot uplift mechanism — you can request a temporary baseline increase with a 7-day notice to activate and a flexible 30/60 day rollback window. For the formal contract we usually keep a 90-day decommit, but for pilots we can include a carve-out so the first 60 days are treated as a pilot term with a reduced decommit penalty.

Sample recommended ramp schedule (Balanced / Option B) — explicit weeks/months:
  - Month 0 (sign): Baseline 32 GPUs, warm pool 8, burst ceiling 96 (reserved lanes available)
  - Month 1: Monitoring & canary runs for two production models; no baseline change unless 85% sustained utilization
  - Month 3: Conditional step to 40 GPUs if sustained weekly baseline utilization >80% for 4 weeks
  - Month 6: Final step to 48 GPUs contingent on successful model rollout & throughput targets

Activation & deactivation triggers (examples):
  - Utilization: CPU/GPU sustained >80% for 2 weeks + latency SLO breaches
  - Feature launch: Product signals a new release with planned expansion window (documented in mutual action plan)
  - Business event: Planned release day or batch scoring window

SLA and penalties: the attached SLA-terms.pdf covers availability commitments for committed lanes (99.95% monthly uptime target for baseline lanes) and credits for sustained outages. Burst lanes are best-effort but we provide failure-mode fallbacks to lower-cost variants if capacity is unavailable.

If Option B looks good we can: 1) lock pricing & draft LOI, 2) provision a pilot uplift window, and 3) schedule a kickoff for technical onboarding (we typically allocate an onboarding engineer + solutions architect for the first 6 weeks).

—Marcus
